newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF pays 47.4 bln yen to private sector in Feb.
newsitem.headline: MOF pays 47.4 bln yen to private sector in Feb.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) paid out 47.4 billion yen to the private sector in February through its special foreign exchange account, MOF data showed on Monday.
The ministry manages Japan's external reserves, which stood at $217.14 billion at the end of January, the world's largest.

The payments, in yen, are from the foreign exchange account to the private sector and are made for such purposes as dollar-buying intervention for yen. But bankers said there was no trace of such intervention this month. Analysts said the payments in February were related to the redemption of 50 billion worth of financing bills (FBs) which had been sold to the private sector.
The MOF does not comment on details of such payments.
The private-sector institutions concerned comprise commercial banks, foreign central banks, municipal governments, public funds and quasi-governmental organisations.
